notes: Page 2 is an introduction page (history of Billund Airport and a photo of the real building). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
The parts list was received with this page. The next building page continues from id b1.
Page 3 only has two photos (airport terminal interior and an aerial view). It has no building step, so nothing was added. The next piece id is still b1.
Page 4 is the Danish version of the introduction text, with a photo of a LEGO store. It has no building step, so nothing was added. The next piece id is still b1.
Page 5 only has two photos (a plane at a jet bridge and an aerial view of the airport). It has no building step, so nothing was added. The next piece id is still b1.
Step 1: black 6x12 plate (b1), the model's first piece. Step 2: three black 1x8 tiles (b2-b4) and two 1x1 tiles (b5, b6) go on the plate edges.
The 1x1 tiles in the step 2 callout are not clearly visible in the picture. I assumed they are black 3070b tiles resting on b1 at the open edge positions. Their exact positions are uncertain.
The 1x8 tiles are longer than the 6-stud short side, so the one at the short end overhangs the plate. Each tile rests only on b1 (the plate).
Step 3: a second black 6x12 plate (b7) is placed next to b1, making a 12x12 square base. The 1x8 tiles from step 2 overhang along the join.

It is unclear how b7 clutches the first plate. Tiles have no studs, so I recorded b7 as joined to b1 side by side and in contact with tiles b2 and b4, not resting on anything. Later pages should show how the plates are actually locked together.
Step 4: one plain black 1x8 tile (b8) goes on the back long edge and the printed 'Billund Airport' 1x8 tile (b9) on the front long edge. Both bridge the two base plates b1 and b7.

The view looks like the base seen from underneath, with the tiles on the same side as the plate studs. I treated the tiles as clutching both plates, so they lock the two plates together. Part of each tile hangs off the end, as drawn.
Because of the unclear orientation, the rests_on lists are my best reading of the picture.

Step 5: a third black 6x12 plate (b10) is added next to b7, on the end where tiles b8 and b9 overhang. It clutches those two overhanging tiles, so I recorded it as joined to b8 and b9. It touches b7 along the seam.
As on earlier pages, the orientation of the tiles relative to the plates is unclear, so these joins are a best reading of the picture.
Step 6: two black 1x8 tiles (b11, b12) go on the two long edges of the newest plate b10, with their free ends overhanging for the next plate. Both tiles are listed as joined to b10 only.
The tiles are 8 long and the edges are 12 long, so they probably also touch b7 and the earlier tiles. The picture does not show it clearly, so I did not add those joins.

Step 7: the fourth and last black 6x12 plate (b13) is added on the end where tiles b11 and b12 overhang. The base is now four plates, 12 x 24 studs, framed by the black tiles. The 4 plates in the parts list are now all used.
As on earlier pages, b13 is recorded as joined to the overhanging tiles b11 and b12, and in contact with b10 along the seam.
Step 8: one black 1x8 tile (b14) and two black 1x1 tiles (b15, b16) finish the border on the open short end of the base, over the last plate b13.

I assumed the 1x1 tiles are black 3070b, matching the border. With b5 and b6 from step 2, all four black 1x1 tiles are now placed. All seven black 1x8 plain tiles are placed too, plus the printed one.

Step 9: a row of 11 light bluish gray 2x2 pieces along the back long edge, inside the black border. They alternate 2x2 tile (b17, b19, ... b27) and jumper plate with centre stud (b18, b20, ... b26), starting and ending with a tile. That is 6 tiles and 5 jumpers, matching the callout.

I put the plates in this order along the length, from the left end: b13, b10, b7, b1. Each plate covers 6 studs of the length. The rests_on lists come from which plate lies under each 2x2 piece in that row, so pieces over a plate seam rest on two plates.
The picture does not show which plate is under each piece, so these are my best reading. The row leaves 1 stud of border at each end.

Step 10: a one-stud-deep row in front of the 2x2 row from step 9, filling its 22-stud length. It has 5 tan 1x2 plates (b28-b32) in front of the 5 jumpers, 5 dark bluish gray 1x2 tiles (b33-b37) and 2 dark bluish gray 1x1 tiles (b38, b39) in front of the 2x2 tiles.

The picture does not make clear which gap gets the two 1x1 tiles. I put them at the left end, over plate b13. The rests_on lists come from the 6-stud plate positions, with seam-crossing pieces resting on two plates. This is a best-guess layout.
These pieces butt against the step 9 pieces and rest only on the black plates, so the step 9 pieces are not in their rests_on lists.

Step 11: a row of grey tiles (four 1x3 b42-b45, one 1x2 b46, two 1x1 b47-b48), one orange 1x1 plate (b40) and one green 1x3 plate (b41, right end), placed on the black plates in front of the step 10 row.

The picture is hard to read here. The exact order and stud positions are my best reading: I put the orange plate about 40% along the row and the green plate at the right end. The rests_on lists follow from that and the plate order b13, b10, b7, b1.
These pieces rest only on the black base plates, so they are joined to plates only. Check the next pages to see whether they touch the step 10 pieces.

Step 12: a coloured row in front of the grey tile row. From the left it is a green 2x2 plate (b49), a yellow 1x6 (b50), a white 1x4 (b52), a second yellow 1x6 (b51) and a white 1x2 (b53). That is 20 studs in all, ending next to the green 1x3 plate b41 from step 11.
The callout shows the green plate as a 2x2 (the parts list has 2x lego-3022 Green), so I used that type.

The rests_on lists follow my reading of which black plate lies under each piece: from the left b13, b10, b7, b1, so pieces over a seam rest on two plates. The row meets the step 11 pieces side by side, but I did not list them as supports.

Step 13: the next row toward the front. Pieces from the callout: blue 1x2 plate, green 1x2 plate, two green 1x1 plates, a third yellow 1x6, green 1x3 plate, tan 1x2 tile, tan 2x2 corner plate and a light bluish gray 1x2 tile. The picture is dense and angled, so the exact positions are low confidence.

My placement guess: green 1x3 (b59) at the left end, then yellow 1x6 (b58) and the tan corner plate (b61), then in the right half a tan tile (b60), green 1x1 (b56), blue 1x2 (b54), green 1x1 (b57), green 1x2 (b55) and the grey tile (b62). The grey tile is not clearly visible in the picture.
The rests_on lists use the black plate order b13, b10, b7, b1. Some of these pieces may also sit on the step 12 pieces, but I could not confirm it, so I recorded only the black plates.

Step 14: a fourth yellow 1x6 plate (b63), an orange 1x1 plate (b67) and three long grey tiles (b64-b66). The grey tiles look like 1x4 grooved tiles (lego-2431 light bluish gray), the same shape as the '4x' tiles in step 11.

Correction to step 11: the parts list has only 2 light bluish gray lego-63864 (1x3) tiles, but step 11 used four. Those four long grey tiles (b42-b45) were most likely lego-2431 (1x4) tiles. With the three here, that gives all 7 light bluish gray 2431 tiles in the list. b42-b45 should be treated as lego-2431.

The placement in this step is a low-confidence guess. The picture shows the yellow plate and orange plate clearly, but the new grey tiles are hard to find, so I put them in the row at the front right. The rests_on lists use the black plate order b13, b10, b7, b1.

Step 15: fills more of the front area. Pieces: three green 2x3 plates (b68-b70), a green 2x2 plate (b71), a green 1x1 plate (b72), five tan 1x1 tiles (b73-b77), two tan 1x2 plates (b78, b79) and a dark bluish gray 1x2 tile (b80).

My placement: one green 2x3 and the dark tile at the front left; a tan strip of the tan plates and tiles in the middle, below the yellow rows; two green 2x3 plates, the green 2x2 and the green 1x1 at the front right. The dark tile's size is a guess (1x2, with 3 of 8 left in the list).
The positions are low confidence because of the angled view. The rests_on lists use the black plate order b13, b10, b7, b1, and I did not list the earlier coloured plates as supports.

Step 16: fills the remaining bare front area with tiles. Pieces: two tan 1x2 tiles (b81, b82), two dark bluish gray 1x2 tiles (b89, b90), three dark bluish gray 1x4 tiles (b83-b85) and three dark bluish gray 2x2 tiles (b86-b88). The callout sizes match the parts list: 3x 2431 and 3x 3068b in dark bluish gray.

These tiles cover the front rows of black studs, which are the only stud rows left at this point. The exact positions are low confidence, so the rests_on lists just use the black plate order b13, b10, b7, b1 for the stud columns I guessed.
The tan tiles form a path segment toward the front, as in the picture.

Step 17 (5x): each copy is a light bluish gray 1x2 plate with a light bluish gray 1x1 grooved tile on one stud. The plate goes on a jumper's centre stud and also sits on the tan 1x2 plate in front of that jumper, one per jumper: b18, b20, b22, b24, b26 with tan plates b28-b32.
The arrows show the five placements at the five jumper studs in the back row. Which tan plate pairs with which jumper is inferred from the step 10 layout (jumper k with tan plate k).
I put the tile on stud 2 of the plate, the one away from the jumper. The picture shows the tile on one end, but I could not tell which end.

Step 18: a second layer of white plates on top of the yellow and white row from steps 12-13. Callout: three white 1x4 plates (b91-b93), two white 1x3 plates (b94, b95), one white 1x2 plate with door rail (b96), one light bluish gray 1x2 brick (b97) and two small light bluish gray pieces (b98, b99).

The callout shows the 2 white pieces as 1x3, not 1x4. With the 1x4 white plate b52 from step 12 that gives the 4 in the parts list, so I used 3623 (1x3 white) for them. The two small grey pieces look like 1x2 tiles. All 5 light bluish gray 3023 plates are already used, so I used light bluish gray 3069b tiles.

The positions are low confidence. I laid the white plates over the yellow row and the white 1x4 (b52). I put the door-rail plate on the green 1x3 (b41) near the right end, the brick on one white plate and a tile on each of two white plates. The rests_on lists follow that guess.

Step 19: a small sub-assembly built 4 times (the top box says 4x), not yet attached to the model, so there are no external edges. Per copy: white 1x2 brick, 1x2 plate, curved 2x2x2/3 brick, round 1x1 plate, a second 1x2 plate and a 1x1 tile.

Sub-steps 1-4: put a tile on a 1x2 plate (1), attach a small round plate to the underside (2), combine with the curved brick (3), and put it all on the white brick (4). The small drawings are hard to read, so the stacking order (brick, plate, curved brick, round plate, top plate, tile) is a best guess.

Part identification is also uncertain. The curved piece is lego-15068 in light bluish gray (6 in the list, 4 used here). The small round piece is taken as lego-6141 light bluish gray (4 in the list). One 1x2 plate looks light bluish gray and the other white; I assumed 3023 white for the lower plate. Counts do not fully match: all 5 light bluish gray 3023 plates were already used in step 17, so the plate colours may differ from what I recorded.

Page 24 adds no new pieces. It places the four sub-assemblies from step 19 (unit1-unit4) on the model. The arrows point to the 2nd to 5th positions along the back, leaving the first pad (jumper b18) without a unit.

Each unit's white brick sits on the white plates of the second layer near jumpers b20, b22, b24 and b26: unit1 on b92, unit2 on b94, unit3 on b93, unit4 on b95. These matches follow my earlier layout guess and are low confidence.
Step 20 (3x): a white 1x2 brick with a light bluish gray 1x2 grooved tile on top. The three copies are pressed onto the white plates in the gaps between the four step 19 units.

I assumed the gaps are at stud 10-11 (on b92), 14-15 (on b94 and b93) and 18-19 (on b93 and b95). Copy 1 is joined to b92. Copy 2 is joined to b94 by the repeat and to b93 by an extra edge. Copy 3 is joined to b93 by the repeat and to b95 by an extra edge. Low confidence, from the arrows in the picture.

All 7 white 1x2 bricks in the parts list are now used (4 in the units plus these 3). The light bluish gray 3069b count (8 used against 7 in the list) is over by one, which probably means one of my earlier colour or type guesses was wrong.

Step 21: one small stack of 1x2 plates, built as white, grey, white, grey, with a grey 1x2 tile on top. That uses the 2 white plates, 2 grey plates and 1 tile in the callout. It is built in two sub-steps, then placed at the right end of the model.
The stack goes on the right end of the white row. I assumed it sits on the door-rail plate b96, near stud 22-23, which is a guess from the arrow.

The grey plates are shown as light bluish gray 3023, but the parts list's 5 light bluish gray 3023 plates were already used in step 17. The grey plates may be another colour, such as dark bluish gray, with a different list count.
Step 22: a small tower of two light bluish gray 1x1 plates topped by a light bluish gray cheese slope. It goes on the grey 1x2 brick b97 in the middle of the model, which I read as the control tower.

The two small round-looking pieces are taken as lego-3024 light bluish gray plates 1x1 (3 in the list). They could be the 6141 round plates, but all 4 of those were used in step 19. Placing the tower on b97 is a guess from the arrow.

Step 23 (2x): a small post built twice. Each is, from the bottom, a white 1x1 plate, two grey 1x1 plates and a darker grey piece on top. The callout counts are 2x white, 4x grey and 2x darker grey. The two posts are then pushed onto the model beside the control tower.

The part types are guesses, because the grey pieces are tiny and the list counts are tight. I took the 4 grey plates as lego-6141 round plates in light bluish gray and the 2 darker top pieces as lego-3062b round bricks (2 in the list). The 6141 count then overlaps with my step 19 guess, so one of those identifications is probably wrong.
I assumed both posts sit on the yellow 1x6 plate b63 in the middle, from the two arrows.

Step 24: two light bluish gray 1x2 bricks (b108, b109) and one white 1x3 brick (b110) in the middle of the model around the yellow plates. With b97 these are the 3 light bluish gray 3004 bricks in the list.

No arrows are shown, so the placement is a low-confidence guess. I put both grey bricks on the yellow 1x6 plate b63 and the white 1x3 across the two grey bricks. The white 1x3 brick type is lego-3622, the only 1x3 brick in the list.

Step 25 (2x): a stack of three 1x2 plates, grey, white, grey from the bottom. It is built twice (2 white and 4 grey plates in the callout) and each stack is pushed onto one of the two grey 1x2 bricks from step 24: b108 and b109.

The grey plates are drawn as light bluish gray 3023, but the list's 5 light bluish gray 3023 plates were used up in step 17, so their colour may differ from what I recorded. The attachment to b108 and b109 is inferred from the two arrows.

Step 26 (2x): each copy is a light bluish gray 1x1 plate on a small round grey piece. The two copies go on top of the two plate stacks from step 25 (stack1.up and stack2.up), following the two arrows.

The round piece is taken as lego-6141 (round plate with solid stud) and the top as lego-3024 light bluish gray. This is a guess and conflicts with my earlier counts: the 4 light bluish gray 6141 were used in step 19, and only 1 light bluish gray 3024 is left. The round piece may be lego-3062b.

Step 27: a white 1x1 brick with a side stud (b111) gets a clear cheese slope (b112) pressed onto the side stud, as the red arrow in the small box shows. The brick then goes on top at the centre of the model.
The slope looks transparent, so I used Trans-Clear 54200 (12 in the list). I assumed the brick sits on the white 1x3 brick b110, from the single arrow at the middle of the model.
Step 28: two light bluish gray 1x2 plates (b113, b114) are added in the central block, with no arrows or close-up. The picture shows only the result.
My placement is a low-confidence guess. I assumed each plate bridges the white 1x3 brick b110 and one of the step 26 caps (cap1.plate, cap2.plate). I could not confirm this from the picture.
Step 29: two dark bluish gray 2x2 plates (b115, b116) cover the two central blocks. There are no arrows, so the placement is a guess.
I assumed each plate covers one step 28 plate and the step 26 cap plate next to it: b115 on b113 and cap1.plate, b116 on b114 and cap2.plate. Low confidence.

Step 30: a tan 1x2 plate (b117) and a light bluish gray 1x2 plate (b118) are added at the centre block. There are no arrows. I put the tan plate on b115 and the grey plate on b116, from where they appear in the picture. Low confidence.
The tan plate is the 8th and last tan 3023 in the list. The grey plate type is lego-3023 light bluish gray, which again goes over the list's count of 5.
Step 31: the white 3x3 cross plate (b119) goes across the centre block, plus two light bluish gray 1x2 plates (b120, b121). There are no arrows.
I assumed the cross sits on the dark 2x2 plates b115 and b116 and the tan and grey plates b117 and b118. I put one grey 1x2 plate on each dark plate. Low confidence.

Step 32 builds one small sub-assembly (no multiplier shown). It is not attached to the model on this page. It uses a 1x1 plate, two 1x2 plates, a long grey tile, a 1x1 tile, a curved brick and two white 1x1 bricks with a side stud.

The 5 small drawings are hard to read, so this structure is a best guess. The two white side-stud bricks (b122, b123) go under plate b124, the 1x1 plate b125 goes on b124, plate b126 goes on b125 with the 1x1 tile b127 on top, and the curved brick b128 with the long tile b129 goes on top.

The long flat grey piece is taken as lego-63864 (Tile 1 x 3) in light bluish gray, but the list has only 2 of those and step 11 already counted 4. That step 11 identification was probably wrong: those pieces were most likely 1x4 tiles.
Page 38 adds no new pieces. It attaches the step 32 sub-assembly at the left end of the model. The arrow points at the left end of the white row, the first position, which had no unit.
I joined its two white side-stud bricks (b122, b123) to the left white 1x4 plate b91. This is low confidence, because the arrow could also mean the first pad (jumper b18).

Step 33: a white 1x2 plate (b130) gets a grey 1x1 tile on one stud (sub-step 1) and a clear cheese slope on the other stud (sub-step 2). The finished piece goes on the back of the central block, where the arrow points.
I assumed the plate sits on the white cross plate b119 and the slope is on the plate's second stud. The slope is Trans-Clear because it looks transparent. Low confidence on the exact stud positions.
Step 34: two cheese slopes are added at the centre of the model. The callout shows one arrow, to the middle top near the cross plate.

The two slopes look like one clear and one pale, so I assumed Trans-Clear and White (4 white in the list). I put both on the white cross plate b119. The second slope's position is not shown, so low confidence.

Step 35: two long grey tiles (b135, b136), added at the centre of the model with no arrows. I took them as lego-63864 (Tile 1 x 3) in light bluish gray, which gives the 2 in the list. I put both on the white cross plate b119. The exact positions are low confidence.
The long grey item in step 32 (b129) was also typed 63864, so that part is probably a different tile type, such as a 1x2 tile.
Step 36: a light bluish gray 1x2 plate (b137) gets a 1x1 tile (b138) and a long curved 4x1 slope (b139, lego-11153). The finished piece goes on the centre of the model, where the arrow points.

I assumed the tile sits on one stud and the curved piece on the other, and that the plate sits on the white cross plate b119. The small drawings do not show exactly where the tile goes, so low confidence.

Step 37: the same kind of piece as step 36 (1x2 plate, 1x1 tile, curved 4x1 slope), with the curve on the other side. It is a mirror arrangement and goes next to the step 36 piece in the centre. The mirrored curved piece has the same type, lego-11153.
As in step 36, I put the plate on the white cross plate b119, with the tile on stud 1 and the curved slope on stud 2. Low confidence.
Step 38 (2x): a clear cheese slope on a white round 1x1 plate, built twice. The two copies go on the two ends of the central block at the arrows.
I took the round plates as lego-6141 white (4 in the list) and the slopes as Trans-Clear 54200. I assumed the plates sit on the dark 2x2 plates b115 and b116 at either end. Low confidence.

Step 39 (2x): the same piece as step 38, a clear cheese slope on a white round 1x1 plate, built twice more. They go on the two blocks at the back of the central block, at the arrows. That uses all 4 white 6141 plates in the list (2 here, 2 in step 38).
As in step 38, I assumed they sit on the dark 2x2 plates b115 and b116, but they may go on another stud. Low confidence.

Step 40 (2x): a small column built twice. Each is a round 1x1 brick (the cylinder), a round 1x1 plate and a light bluish gray cheese slope on top. The two columns go on the model near the centre front and right of the centre.

I took the cylinder as lego-3062b (2 in the list), the disc as lego-6141 light bluish gray and the slope as light bluish gray 54200. The 6141 count (4 in the list) is probably overcounted by my earlier guesses (steps 19, 23, 26).
I assumed one column sits on yellow plate b63 and the other on dark plate b116, from the two arrow ends. Low confidence.
Step 41 (2x): a white cheese slope on a white 1x1 plate, built twice. The two copies go on the front of the model at the two arrows, one at each end of the central block.
I assumed the plates sit on the white second-layer plates b92 and b95 near the front ends. The picture does not show exactly where they sit, so low confidence.

Step 42 (2x): a long curved 4x1 slope clipped onto the stud of a 1x1 plate (the red arrow shows the plate pushed up into the underside of the curve). It is built twice, and the two copies go at the two arrows, on the model's central block, to make roof ridges. With steps 36-37 that uses all 4 lego-11153 in the list.
I assumed the plates sit on the dark 2x2 plates b115 and b116. The plate is lego-3024 light bluish gray, though only 3 are in the list and my earlier steps overuse them. Low confidence.

Step 43: builds a small white block about 2x2 studs, topped by a grey curved brick, in 5 sub-steps. It is not attached to the model on this page. Parts: 2 white 2x2 plates, 5 white 1x2 plates (shown greyish in the callout, drawn white in the stack) and one light bluish gray curved 2x2 brick.

The layer order is a best guess from the small drawings: 1x2 plates side by side (b143, b144), a 2x2 plate (b145), 1x2 plates (b146, b147), a 2x2 plate (b148), a 1x2 plate (b149), and the curved brick on top (b150). The layer count in the drawings is hard to read.
The 1x2 plate colour is assumed White, from the stack drawing. White 3023 counts in the list (6) are overused by my guesses in other steps.
Page 50 adds no new pieces. It places the step 43 white block with the curved top at the left of the central roof, where the arrow points.
I joined its bottom plates b143 and b144 to the white plates b91 and b92. This is low confidence, because the plates are hidden under other pieces in the picture.
Step 44: two dark green 1x3 plates (b151, b152), two dark green 1x1 plates (b153, b154) and two black round supports (lego-64644, b155, b156). There are no arrows, so I read the result image.

The dark green plates go on the front green plates, one pair at the front left (on b68) and one at the front right (on b69), as trees or hedges. The black round supports stand at the right end of the white plates, as lamp posts. I put them on b93 and b95. All positions are low confidence.

Step 45: three bright green flower plates (24866) on the green plates at the front left, like plants or bushes. No arrows. In the result image two are on the green near the left end and one is lower and to the right. I put them on b59, b59 and b68. Low confidence, but they are single pieces on a stud each.
Step 46: four blue round 1x1 plates (6141) and four bright light orange flower plates (24866), a flower bed on the green plates at the right end. No arrows, so I read the result picture.
I spread the 8 pieces over the right-hand green plates b70, b71 and b72 (b71 is a 2x2, so at most 4 pieces). The exact positions are low confidence.
The step 19 and step 23 guesses already used 6141 plates, so the 4 blue ones here are the only ones I am sure of.

Step 47: four white round 1x1 plates and four bright green flower plates are stacked onto the flower bed from step 46. The picture shows them stacked on the blue and orange pieces. I paired them one to one: white on blue (b160-b163), green flower on orange flower (b164-b167).

That brings the bright green flowers to 7 (3 in step 45 and 4 here), matching the list. The 4 white 6141 here are the real white round plates. The white round plates I used in steps 38-39 may have been a different type, such as 3024.
The exact pairing is a guess, since the cluster is dense.

Step 48: a flagpole. The red clip plate (b177) clips onto the white 3L bar (b176) as the green arrow shows, and the bar stands in a stud at the right end of the model. This is the red flag, as in the box art.
I assumed the bar stands on the green 1x3 plate b41 at the right end, from the arrow position. Low confidence on which stud. The clip can rotate on the bar, so I marked it revolute.

Step 49: a small yellow vehicle, with a black 1x2 plate (b178) as the base. Sub-step 1 puts a grey 1x1 plate (b179) on it, and sub-step 2 adds the yellow pieces: a yellow cheese slope (b181) and a yellow 1x1 tile (b180). The finished piece goes on the far left front of the base, next to the green flowers.

The callout shows two yellow pieces that both look like slopes, but the parts list has only 1 yellow 54200 and 1 yellow 3070b tile. I took the second as the yellow tile. The exact stud positions are low confidence.
I assumed the black plate sits on the black base plate b13 at the left front. This is a guess from the arrow.

Step 50 builds five small aeroplanes, not yet attached to the model. The planes differ, so they are listed separately rather than as a repeat. Each plane has a white 1x3 plate (fuselage), a 1x2 plate (tail), a tail slope, a white 1x3 tile (wing) and a clear cheese slope (cockpit).

The sub-steps show plane A (blue plate, red slope) in detail: a 1x2 plate on two studs of the white 1x3 plate, a tail slope and a wing tile, then the clear slope on the free stud. The other four tail colours follow the callout: B red plate with white slope, C white plate with dark blue slope, D yellow plate with blue slope, E dark azure plate with white slope.
How the tile (wing) attaches is a guess: I recorded it joined to the tail plate. The callout also shows 5 white 1x3 plates and 5 white 1x3 tiles.
Page 58 adds no new pieces. It places the five aeroplanes from step 50 along the back edge, one on each of the five pads from step 17 (the light bluish gray plates on the jumper studs).

Step 1: black 6x12 plate (b1), the model's first piece. Step 2: three black 1x8 tiles (b2-b4) and two 1x1 tiles (b5, b6) go on the plate edges.
The 1x1 tiles in the step 2 callout are not clearly visible in the picture. I assumed they are black 3070b tiles resting on b1 at the open edge positions. Their exact positions are uncertain.
The 1x8 tiles are longer than the 6-stud short side, so the one at the short end overhangs the plate. Each tile rests only on b1 (the plate).
Step 3: a second black 6x12 plate (b7) is placed next to b1, making a 12x12 square base. The 1x8 tiles from step 2 overhang along the join.

It is unclear how b7 clutches the first plate. Tiles have no studs, so I recorded b7 as joined to b1 side by side and in contact with tiles b2 and b4, not resting on anything. Later pages should show how the plates are actually locked together.
Step 4: one plain black 1x8 tile (b8) goes on the back long edge and the printed 'Billund Airport' 1x8 tile (b9) on the front long edge. Both bridge the two base plates b1 and b7.

The view looks like the base seen from underneath, with the tiles on the same side as the plate studs. I treated the tiles as clutching both plates, so they lock the two plates together. Part of each tile hangs off the end, as drawn.
Because of the unclear orientation, the rests_on lists are my best reading of the picture.

Step 5: a third black 6x12 plate (b10) is added next to b7, on the end where tiles b8 and b9 overhang. It clutches those two overhanging tiles, so I recorded it as joined to b8 and b9. It touches b7 along the seam.
As on earlier pages, the orientation of the tiles relative to the plates is unclear, so these joins are a best reading of the picture.
Step 6: two black 1x8 tiles (b11, b12) go on the two long edges of the newest plate b10, with their free ends overhanging for the next plate. Both tiles are listed as joined to b10 only.
The tiles are 8 long and the edges are 12 long, so they probably also touch b7 and the earlier tiles. The picture does not show it clearly, so I did not add those joins.

Step 7: the fourth and last black 6x12 plate (b13) is added on the end where tiles b11 and b12 overhang. The base is now four plates, 12 x 24 studs, framed by the black tiles. The 4 plates in the parts list are now all used.
As on earlier pages, b13 is recorded as joined to the overhanging tiles b11 and b12, and in contact with b10 along the seam.
Step 8: one black 1x8 tile (b14) and two black 1x1 tiles (b15, b16) finish the border on the open short end of the base, over the last plate b13.

I assumed the 1x1 tiles are black 3070b, matching the border. With b5 and b6 from step 2, all four black 1x1 tiles are now placed. All seven black 1x8 plain tiles are placed too, plus the printed one.

Step 9: a row of 11 light bluish gray 2x2 pieces along the back long edge, inside the black border. They alternate 2x2 tile (b17, b19, ... b27) and jumper plate with centre stud (b18, b20, ... b26), starting and ending with a tile. That is 6 tiles and 5 jumpers, matching the callout.

I put the plates in this order along the length, from the left end: b13, b10, b7, b1. Each plate covers 6 studs of the length. The rests_on lists come from which plate lies under each 2x2 piece in that row, so pieces over a plate seam rest on two plates.
The picture does not show which plate is under each piece, so these are my best reading. The row leaves 1 stud of border at each end.

The picture does not make clear which gap gets the two 1x1 tiles. I put them at the left end, over plate b13. The rests_on lists come from the 6-stud plate positions, with seam-crossing pieces resting on two plates. This is a best-guess layout.
These pieces butt against the step 9 pieces and rest only on the black plates, so the step 9 pieces are not in their rests_on lists.

Step 11: a row of grey tiles (four 1x3 b42-b45, one 1x2 b46, two 1x1 b47-b48), one orange 1x1 plate (b40) and one green 1x3 plate (b41, right end), placed on the black plates in front of the step 10 row.

The picture is hard to read here. The exact order and stud positions are my best reading: I put the orange plate about 40% along the row and the green plate at the right end. The rests_on lists follow from that and the plate order b13, b10, b7, b1.
These pieces rest only on the black base plates, so they are joined to plates only. Check the next pages to see whether they touch the step 10 pieces.

Step 13: the next row toward the front. Pieces from the callout: blue 1x2 plate, green 1x2 plate, two green 1x1 plates, a third yellow 1x6, green 1x3 plate, tan 1x2 tile, tan 2x2 corner plate and a light bluish gray 1x2 tile. I assumed the bar stands on the green 1x3 plate b41 at the right end, from the arrow position. Low confidence on which stud. The clip can rotate on the bar, so I marked it revolute.

I assumed the black plate sits on the black base plate b13 at the left front. This is a guess from the arrow.
